title: The Unsafe Gate
goal: boost() is marked unsafe - the caller must say the word, out loud.
hints: Calling an unsafe fn is one of the five things only an unsafe block may do.
The block is a signature - you, the caller, accepting the function's safety contract.
explanation: Calling an unsafe fn outside an unsafe block is E0133 - the language insists the caller acknowledge the contract, visibly and greppably. `unsafe { boost() }` is that acknowledgment: you've read boost's # Safety section and vouch for its preconditions here. Note the optimal score is one unsafe block, not zero - when unsafety is genuinely required, the goal is owning it explicitly, not pretending it away. (And `unsafe boost()` without braces isn't syntax - unsafe delimits a block, not a keyword you sprinkle on a call.)
